summary: Hosea pays fifteen pieces of silver, a homer of barley and a lethek of barley. The repeated word for barley identifies what each measure contains.

senses.definition: A measure of dry produce, used of barley in the only biblical occurrence.

evidence.note: The lethek is a second quantity of barley alongside the homer in the purchase price.

note: The traditional reckoning makes the lethek half a kor. Hosea names the two grain quantities without giving their ratio. The Aramaic term may reflect borrowing.
